adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricated `-ms-align-items` property in align-items mixin (mixins.scss:113) does not exist in any IE implementation; it compiles silently and deceptively suggests IE10 legacy support that is only actually provided by the `-ms-flex-align` line
order mixin applied to header.scss `.panel` and `.extra-info-wrapper` without fallback positioning when `display: flex` is unsupported, since floats were removed

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.panel` had `float: right;` removed and now relies on flex behavior (`margin-left: auto;` plus `@include order(3);`), while `.contents` was switched to `@include flexbox()`. If flexbox (and the vendor-prefixed variants) isn’t supported, the previous right-aligned positioning via float no longer exists, so layout could regress in non-flex browsers. However, the finding is less accurate for `.extra-info-wrapper`: the diff only adds `@include order(2);` and does not remove any float/positioning there, so the “floats were removed” claim doesn’t apply to that selector based on this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `align-items(baseline)` from badges.css.scss becomes an invalid value for `-webkit-box-align` in the 2009 spec (which only accepts start|end|center|baseline|stretch), causing legacy WebKit to silently drop it and render badge rows with default alignment

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `@include align-items(baseline);` expands via the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` to `-webkit-box-align: baseline;` (plus other properties). Under the 2009 flexbox spec, `-webkit-box-align` explicitly accepts `baseline` (along with start|end|center|stretch), so this is not an invalid value and there’s no diff-grounded basis for claiming legacy WebKit would drop it due to invalidity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RTL layout requirement is silently dropped: order(2)/order(3) numeric values are not flipped by the RTL CSS pipeline like float left/right were, breaking header layout for RTL-language forums

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces direction-sensitive floats (`.title { float: left; }`, `.panel { float: right; }`) with flexbox layout and fixed ordering (`@include order(2)`, `@include order(3)`) plus `margin-left: auto`. If the project previously relied on an RTL CSS pipeline that automatically flipped left/right floats, this change could require explicit RTL handling for `order()` and `margin-left` to preserve mirrored layout. However, the diff alone does not show the RTL pipeline behavior or requirements, so the RTL breakage cannot be conclusively verified from the patch itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Invalid property -ms-align-items in mixins.scss:108 is not a real IE flexbox property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align), resulting in dead code and silent fallback to stretch in legacy-IE builds

Removed .bullet margin-top: 5px offset with no replacement; generic line-height: 1.5 compensation applies to all badge-wrapper styles and does not restore bullet glyph vertical alignment with the topic title

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the specific rule `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper { &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; } }` in `topic.scss` with no direct replacement targeted at `.badge-wrapper.bullet`. It only adds `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper`, which affects all content there, not specifically the bullet badge. Whether this causes a visible vertical misalignment regression can’t be verified from the diff alone, but the concern is diff-grounded and actionable as a potential UI regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Small-actions rendered without a topic-avatar lose their visual rhythm: the 4em left indent is deleted and margin-top/padding-top offsets are gone, with only padding: 0 1.5% remaining

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the previous spacing that created the left indent and vertical offsets in `.small-action-desc` (from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%;`), and also removes `padding-top: 4px` and changes inner `p` margins to `0`. That supports the claim that the “rhythm”/indent is gone. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove this is a defect specifically when there is no `.topic-avatar` (it may be an intentional flexbox refactor), so it’s a concrete, diff-grounded UI regression concern rather than a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Header .contents children other than title/extra-info/panel remain at implicit order: 0, so any plugin-injected or prepended element renders before the panel, silently changing header ordering because order values are hardcoded per-selector

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed into a flex container (`@include flexbox();`) and `.panel` is given an explicit flex order (`@include order(3);`) plus `margin-left: auto;`. No explicit `order` is shown here for other potential `.contents` children (e.g., `.title` no longer floats and has no order set in this diff), so any additional/prepended elements inside `.contents` would remain at the default `order: 0` and therefore render before the `.panel` in visual order. That’s a real compatibility/extension risk created by this change, though the diff alone doesn’t prove such plugin-injected elements exist in this codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .small-action-desc padding/margin restyle in topic-post.scss (padding: 0 1.5%, margin: 0, removal of padding-top: 4px) is not traceable to the stated header layout performance intent and belongs in a separate commit/PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the `.small-action-desc` restyle in `topic-post.scss` (padding changed to `0 1.5%`, paragraph margin set to `0`, `padding-top: 4px` removed). However, the finding’s claim that this is “not traceable to the stated header layout performance intent” and therefore “belongs in a separate commit/PR” depends on external context (PR description/intent) that is not present in the diff. From the diff alone, we can’t verify what the stated intent was or whether these changes are out of scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .extra-info-wrapper line-height: 1.5 and removal of .bullet { margin-top: 5px } in topic.scss is a visual change out of scope for the flexbox conversion and changes rendering of every child, risking single-line title height regressions

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `topic.scss` does introduce broader visual/layout changes beyond adding flexbox ordering: it adds `line-height: 1.5;` to `.extra-info-wrapper` (affecting all text/inline children) and removes the nested `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule. These are real, diff-grounded style changes that can alter rendering/vertical alignment and may be out of scope for a pure flexbox conversion, but they are not a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss emits invalid -ms-align-items property (correct 2012 syntax is -ms-flex-align, already present), shipping a dead/invalid declaration to every call site and causing CSS bloat
matched_golden_ids: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the use of the invalid legacy property `-ms-align-items` and notes the correct 2012 IE/Edge syntax is `-ms-flex-align` (already present). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment (that `-ms-align-items` never existed and should be `-ms-flex-align`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The .valign-helper hack is retained in header.scss while its purpose is superseded by align-items(center), adding unnecessary line-height to every header render and risking double-offset centering if floats are later removed without the helper

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss` the `.contents` container is changed to use flexbox with `@include align-items(center);`, but the `.valign-helper` rule block remains in the file unchanged. The diff supports a review point that an older vertical-alignment helper may now be redundant/conflicting after switching to flex alignment, though the specific claim about it adding line-height/double-offset isn’t directly verifiable from the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flexbox() mixin's 2009 old-box fallback (display: -webkit-box; display: -moz-box) breaks right-alignment of .panel on old engines because old-box layout doesn't honor margin-left: auto and floats were removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `float: right` from `.panel` and relies on `margin-left: auto` inside a new flex container (`.contents` now uses `@include flexbox()`). But `flexbox()` includes 2009-era fallbacks (`display: -webkit-box; display: -moz-box;`) for engines that don’t support modern flexbox. In those old “box” implementations, `margin-left: auto` is not a reliable/right-way to push an item to the end (typically you’d need box-pack/box-flex patterns), so `.panel` can lose its right-alignment specifically on those old engines the fallback targets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Converting .contents to a flex container silently disables float-based layout for any remaining/theme/plugin-inserted children that rely on float

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.contents` in `header.scss` from a normal block container to a flex container via `@include flexbox()` and `@include align-items(center)`, while also removing the explicit float-based layout on `.title` and `.panel`. In a flex formatting context, `float` on flex items does not participate in float layout (it effectively won’t float), so any other children inside `.contents`—including theme/plugin-inserted elements—that relied on float-based positioning could be affected. The diff doesn’t show such children, so the breakage isn’t directly verifiable here, but the compatibility risk is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: @include order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper is dead code because it's not a direct child of .contents; order only applies to flex items

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `.extra-info-wrapper { @include order(2); ... }` being added in `topic.scss`, but it does not show the HTML structure or the parent container styles that would determine whether `.extra-info-wrapper` is a flex item. The claim that it is "not a direct child of .contents" cannot be verified from these changes, and `.contents` in `header.scss` appears unrelated to `topic.scss`. Therefore the finding asserts context not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: order(3) on .panel is redundant given margin-left: auto and only matters on broken old-spec engines, making it misleading dead code

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.contents` becoming a flex container and `.panel` gaining both `margin-left: auto;` and `@include order(3);`, but it does not show the DOM order or other flex items’ ordering. `order` is not inherently redundant with `margin-left: auto` (it affects item sequence, not alignment), and nothing in the diff proves it only matters on “broken old-spec engines” or is dead/misleading code in this context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items() mixin emits nonexistent -ms-align-items property, and hand-maintained prefix lines will map modern keywords like flex-start to engines (2009 -webkit-box-align, IE10 -ms-flex-align) that reject them, producing partially-applied alignment

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `@mixin align-items($alignment)` that emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a valid IE flexbox property (IE uses `-ms-flex-align`). The mixin also directly forwards modern alignment keywords into legacy-prefixed properties like `-webkit-box-align`/`-ms-flex-align`, which can reject values such as `flex-start`/`flex-end`, leading to prefixed engines ignoring the alignment and producing inconsistent layout. This is a defect in the newly added mixin code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Making .small-action a flex container lays children (button, .small-action-desc) side-by-side in a row instead of stacked, breaking multi-line descriptions and multi-child small-action variants on narrow widths

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox();` with no `flex-direction`/`flex-wrap`), so children will lay out in a row by default. However, the finding’s premise that the layout was intended to be “stacked” is not supported by the diff: previously `.small-action-desc` had `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em`, which already implies a side-by-side/indented layout (e.g., accommodating an avatar to the left), not a stacked one. Whether this breaks multi-line descriptions or narrow widths can’t be verified from the diff alone (no HTML/structure shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Restyling of .small-action internals (.small-action-desc padding, p margins, padding-top removal) is a visual redesign unrelated to the stated 'flexbox performance' PR objective, shipped without design sign-off

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show visual style changes inside `.small-action` (e.g., `.small-action-desc` padding changed, paragraph margins set to `0`, `padding-top` removed). However, the finding’s key assertions—being “unrelated to the stated 'flexbox performance' PR objective” and “shipped without design sign-off”—cannot be verified from the diff alone because the PR objective/sign-off context is not present in the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deletion of the .title rule and converting .contents to a flex container changes rendering of descendants relying on block flow (title wrapping, text-overflow ellipsis, full-width children) with no test or note

adjudication.rationale: In header.scss, `.contents` is changed into a flex container via `@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`, and the standalone `.title { float: left; }` rule is removed. Also `.panel` stops floating and instead uses `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)`. These are substantial layout mechanics changes that can affect wrapping/ellipsis/width behavior of children compared to normal block/float flow, but the diff itself doesn’t prove a concrete defect—just a potentially risky visual change with no accompanying note or verification in the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: line-height: 1.5 added to .extra-info-wrapper and removal of .badge-wrapper.bullet margin-top compensation is an unverified visual change; badges may be double-compensated or misaligned

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce intentional visual/layout changes in `.extra-info-wrapper`: it adds `line-height: 1.5` and removes the prior `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` adjustment. Those changes can affect vertical alignment/spacing of bullet-style badges, but the claim that badges "may be double-compensated or misaligned" is speculative and not directly verifiable from the diff alone. It’s still a concrete, diff-grounded “please visually verify” concern rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rewrite of &.bullet using mixins is not behavior-preserving: -webkit-box-align baseline has different legacy semantics and -ms-align-items is dead code, causing misaligned bullet badges on legacy webkit browsers

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `&.bullet` changes from `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline;` to using `@include inline-flex();` and `@include align-items(baseline);`, which still emit the unprefixed `inline-flex` and `align-items: baseline` declarations. The finding’s claim that this is definitively “not behavior-preserving” and “caus[es] misaligned bullet badges on legacy webkit browsers” is not verifiable from the diff alone; it asserts a specific runtime misalignment without evidence. While `-ms-align-items` in the mixin is likely redundant/invalid, that alone doesn’t prove a behavior regression in the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .panel order(3) and .extra-info-wrapper order(2) spread across files with magic numbers and no source of truth; subsequent child reordering silently shuffles visual order

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces hardcoded flex ordering via `@include order(3);` on `.panel` in `header.scss` and `@include order(2);` on `.extra-info-wrapper` in `topic.scss`, using numeric “magic numbers” without a shared variable/commented convention. While not a direct defect, this is a maintainability/architecture concern because visual order becomes dependent on scattered numeric values and can be unintentionally changed when other flex children add/modify `order`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .small-action becoming display:flex with removed padding-left: 4em changes avatar/description layout, meaning the PR delivers a multi-component visual redesign beyond its stated performance objective without acceptance of visual deltas

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the `.small-action` layout from non-flex to flex (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and removes the large left padding on `.small-action-desc` (from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%`), plus adjusts inner `p` margins. Those changes are likely to materially alter avatar/description positioning and spacing, raising a concrete visual-regression/scope concern. However, claims about the PR’s stated objective or lack of acceptance for visual deltas are not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New behavior-bearing SCSS code (four new mixins and layout changes like .title/.panel float→flex) has no verification mechanism—no visual regression snapshot or render test in the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces behavior-affecting layout changes (e.g., header.scss replaces .title/.panel floats with flexbox via @include flexbox()/align-items()/order(), topic-post.scss changes spacing/margins, and adds new flexbox-related mixins in mixins.scss), but the PR diff contains only SCSS changes and no accompanying UI/visual verification artifacts (e.g., screenshot snapshots, render/feature specs) to guard against regressions from these layout changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: -moz-inline-box and -ms-align-items are invalid property names that Sass will emit verbatim as dead declarations, potentially causing misaligned category bullets on browsers honoring only unprefixed flex

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `-moz-inline-box` appears as a **value** for the `display` property (`display: -moz-inline-box;`), not a property name, so the finding misstates that. The mixin does introduce `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a standard flexbox property (IE uses `-ms-flex-align`), but an extra unknown declaration is simply ignored by browsers and the diff also emits the correct unprefixed `align-items: $alignment;`. The claim that this would “potentially cause misaligned category bullets on browsers honoring only unprefixed flex” is not supported by what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of the .badge-wrapper.bullet margin compensation is unverified and could cause misalignment

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic.scss`, within `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper`, the nested `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule was removed. The finding’s concern (potential visual misalignment/regression due to removing a prior margin compensation) is grounded in the diff, but the diff alone cannot verify whether alignment is now correct (other flex/order changes may compensate).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No compile-output or snapshot check exists to guard against invalid emitted CSS in this project

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows SCSS changes (adding flexbox-related mixins and using them in several stylesheets). It does not show anything about CI, build steps, CSS compilation, or snapshot/compile-output checks, so the claim that "no compile-output or snapshot check exists" cannot be verified from this PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Old-flexbox vendor fallbacks (-moz-box, -ms-flexbox, -webkit-box): margin-left: auto as a push-right replacement for float: right is not honored by 2009-spec -moz-box/-webkit-box implementations, so .panel may not right-align on legacy engines; the prefixed declarations are also dead weight

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.panel` stops using `float: right` and instead relies on `margin-left: auto` inside a flex container (`.contents` now has `@include flexbox()`). The new `flexbox()` mixin emits 2009-era `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` fallbacks, but those legacy implementations do not consistently support auto-margins as a right-alignment mechanism the way modern flexbox does. This can cause `.panel` to no longer right-align in browsers that pick the `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` path, making it a behavior regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: -ms-align-items in align-items() mixin (mixins.scss:120) is not a real property in any engine — dead declaration line

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `@mixin align-items($alignment)` (mixins.scss), the line `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` is present alongside the correct IE flexbox form `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;`. `-ms-align-items` is not a recognized prefixed property for any major engine, so it’s a dead/ineffective declaration. This is a concrete, diff-grounded cleanup issue rather than a functional defect (it doesn’t break behavior since other valid declarations remain).

adjudication_records.issue_text: .valign-helper becomes a flex item when .contents is converted to a flex row, breaking the inline/table cell based vertical alignment hack for the title

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed into a flex container via `@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);` (and the old float-based `.title` rule is removed). If `.valign-helper` is a child element inside `.contents` (as its naming/placement suggests in this header block), it will now participate as a flex item, which can invalidate the prior inline/table-cell vertical-alignment hack. This is a concrete behavior change introduced by the diff, though the exact DOM nesting isn’t shown here.
